transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is I’m just… exhausted. Like, worn out all the time. I can be in bed a full night and still wake up feeling like my body is made of sandbags.

It’s making normal stuff feel ridiculous—getting through a workday, or even folding laundry, takes everything I’ve got. And I know everyone’s tired, I mean, my coworkers are always joking about needing coffee, and I do market research so there are these long stretches of staring at spreadsheets and survey comments, which would make anybody tired—but this feels heavier than that. I just don’t feel like I’m getting my energy back.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. Most days I wake up and there’s this heavy, flat feeling right here, like in my chest. It’s not even always crying or anything dramatic, it’s more like everything is gray before the day even starts.

Sometimes I’ll just sit at the kitchen table with my coffee and stare out at the yard, and I’ll notice the neighbor’s dog running around or the weeds coming up by the fence—I keep meaning to deal with those—and I just get this feeling like… I don’t know, like there isn’t some better version of things waiting up ahead. Like no good version of the future is coming.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with others?

Yeah, definitely. I used to be really good about making time for things—hiking on weekends, yoga, messing around in my garden. I have this camera I bought mostly for taking bird pictures, because there’s this one little spot near the trail where I’d always see cardinals and sometimes hawks, and I’d get kind of excited about it.

But lately I just… don’t. I’ll think about going, or I’ll even tell someone I might, and then I cancel or just don’t follow through. The camera’s been sitting in the closet, and the garden is kind of embarrassing right now. It all feels like too much effort, and not in a “busy” way—more like I can’t convince myself it’s worth doing.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… I’d say about two months, maybe since we took on the mortgage. That’s when it really seemed to shift.

Before that I was in this weird overcharged “business push” mode, like trying to get everything handled and making plans, and then after the mortgage stuff settled in, I just kind of dropped into this low stretch. It’s hard to pin down exactly because time’s been kind of blurry, but… yeah, around two months.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or maybe feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… more slow, I think. My husband actually said the other day that I move around the house like I’m underwater, which annoyed me at first, but… he’s not wrong.

Like he’ll ask me something simple—where I put the mail, or if I want him to pick something up—and I know I heard him, but it takes me a while to answer. The words feel like they’re stuck somewhere. I’ll just stand there, and then by the time I say it, it comes out really slow. It’s embarrassing.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot more or a lot less than usual?

I don’t think so? Not in a way I’ve really tracked. I mean, some days I forget to eat lunch and then I’ll just have cereal or whatever’s easiest, but I’ve always been kind of bad about meals when my routine gets thrown off.

Weight-wise, I haven’t noticed anything dramatic. My jeans fit about the same, I think. Although I did buy this one pair online that fit weird, but that might just be the brand—my sister keeps telling me not to order clothes from those random ads, and she’s probably right.

So… no, I don’t think there’s been a big appetite or weight change.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

I… yeah. I haven’t really wanted to say that out loud.

It’s not like I have a plan or anything, I don’t. But late at night, when my husband’s asleep and the house is quiet, I’ll start thinking maybe he’d be better off without me. And then I get stuck on it, like it loops around even when I’m trying not to think about it.

I know that sounds dramatic—I mean, I was literally worrying about whether we bought the wrong kind of blinds for the living room last week, and then my brain goes to that, which makes no sense—but it scares me that the thought keeps coming back.
Have you had any specific plans or intentions about how you would hurt yourself?

No… no specific plan. I haven’t gotten that far, or—sorry, that sounds strange. I mean I haven’t sat down and thought, “I’m going to do this” or picked a way.

It’s more late at night, when everything’s quiet, I start thinking my husband might be better off without me. Then it kind of sticks, like a song you can’t get out of your head, except obviously much worse. I’ll try to distract myself, and then I’m thinking about something random like whether I left dishes in the sink, and then it comes back again.

But I don’t have an intention to do it. The fact that it keeps coming back is what scares me.
Have you noticed that you no longer take pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even things that used to make you happy or relaxed?

Yeah… I think so. I used to make time for things that felt like they sort of reset me—hiking, yoga, messing around in the garden, taking pictures of birds. I even bought this little lens attachment thing once because I was convinced I was going to get better at it, and then I mostly took blurry photos of robins.

But lately I just… don’t. I’ll tell myself I should go for a walk or pull weeds or take the camera out, and then it feels like this huge amount of effort for something that won’t really matter. I keep canceling plans or letting the camera sit in the closet. It’s not that I hate those things now, exactly. They just don’t feel worth starting.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or unusually irritable for several days or more?

Yeah… there was a stretch like that. It was right after we signed the mortgage papers, those first few weeks.

I remember feeling almost… lit up, like I could handle everything and nothing was going to slow me down. Which is funny because buying a house is supposed to make you exhausted, right? There are all these forms and inspections and people emailing you things with “urgent” in the subject line—sorry, I’m getting off track.

But yes, I felt unusually energized, almost unstoppable at times. And then the next minute I’d be really irritable. Like I’d snap at my husband over some tiny delay, or get short with coworkers if something wasn’t moving fast enough. At the time I thought I was just stressed from the mortgage stuff, but looking back it did feel… different from my normal stress.
